concept.title: SVG
concept.shortdesc: With SVG you draw shapes, curves, gradients and text. CSSMedia draws them as vector graphics in the PDF, so they stay sharp at any size. This chapter explains how to put a drawing in your document, how to style it and which parts of SVG you can use. The SVG reference at the end lists the properties and elements.

conbody.p: A drawing is a tree of elements, written in XML. It can be part of your own XML, or it can be a file that an element shows as an image. In both cases CSSMedia reads the drawing, applies the style sheets that reach it and writes the result as lines, curves and text in the PDF. Nothing becomes a bitmap, and the text of a drawing stays text.
SVG elements belong to a namespace, so every svg element declares it:
conbody.pre: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="60"> <rect width="120" height="60" fill="#cfe3f5"/> </svg>
conbody.p: A drawing has its own coordinate system. Its origin is the top left corner, the x axis goes to the right and the y axis goes down. One unit of this system, a user unit, is one CSS pixel. The viewBox attribute changes the scale, as Put a drawing in your document shows.
The element names are fixed by SVG. These are the elements that CSSMedia draws or uses:

row.entry: Holds a drawing. Inside another drawing, it makes a nested drawing with its own size and scale.
rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path
Group shapes, define shapes that are drawn later, and repeat them.

Defines a mark that is drawn at the vertices of a shape.

Write text, in a line, along a path or inside a shape.

Holds a style sheet for the drawing.

conbody.p: The elements title, desc and metadata describe a drawing and are not drawn.
The elements of SVG that are for screens, such as animate and script, have no effect in a PDF.

A drawing uses the same CSS as the rest of your document. Properties such as fill and stroke are CSS properties, and the style sheet of your document reaches the elements of a drawing that is part of your XML. The topics of this chapter follow the work of making a drawing:
